limitations: Hosted GitHub controls/alerts, remote-only refs, advisory services, package registries, cloud tenants, live providers, organizational policies, and fresh authoritative standards retrieval were not authorized or queried.
ESLint, a configured JavaScript type checker, PSScriptAnalyzer, and a local Bicep security/semantic validation result are unavailable; syntax checks are not substitutes.
No C#, Python, TypeScript, or other compiled-language application source is present in the committed baseline. Their instruction files do not establish native analyzer coverage.
Unreachable/pruned objects, forks, remote PR refs, hosted Actions logs/artifacts/releases/packages, issues/discussions/wikis, and caches outside approved local scope remain unassessed.
Manual analysis is trust-boundary and call-path focused, not a claim that every possible execution, concurrency race, browser/device state, or external service behavior was exhaustively explored.
No source remediation, installation, credential validation, cloud operation, commit, push, publication, event-history rewrite, or approval-state transition was performed.
The 26 pending worktree entries are separately inspected as deltas; the full gate applies to committed source only. Report outputs are the audit's permitted changes.

The full gate recorded 925 passed, 29 failed, and 4 skipped on Node 24.22.2/npm 11.19.1. The foreground terminal later resolved Node 26.13.0; one affected case and standalone verification passed there. Runtime drift was observed, but the null subprocess statuses were not conclusively diagnosed or treated as source defects.
This audit's reviewed-analysis phase does not replace the independently authored security-review approval required by the formal release policy.
